title: An exceptional observation of a supermassive black hole directing jets of plasma towards Earth
excerpt: Washington – Astronomers have been able to track the activity of a supermassive black hole for 27 years, in a long-term study that has revealed new details about its plasma jets.
content:
• supermassive black holes
  • A long journey through space

Washington, DC – Astronomers have tracked the activity of a supermassive black hole for 27 years in a long-term study that has revealed new details about the jets of plasma ejected from the celestial body toward Earth.

The tracking is based on relatively continuous observations of the black hole’s activity.

This has allowed researchers to compare changes in the jets over many years and to study how they move and evolve in space.

These jets form when matter accumulates around supermassive black holes in hot disks known as accretion disks.

Simultaneously, some of the matter and energy can be ejected from the black hole’s vicinity as high-speed jets of particles and plasma.

This type of object is of particular interest to astronomers because studying jets helps us

understand the physical processes occurring in the extremely gravitational environments surrounding black holes.

Furthermore, it contributes to our understanding of the nature of the magnetic fields that can influence the movement of matter and energy.

Long-term observations have demonstrated the importance of monitoring these phenomena over extended periods.

Comparing older and more recent observations can reveal changes

that are not readily apparent when studying a celestial object over a short timeframe.

A long journey through space

Scientists point out that the jet’s trajectory toward Earth does not necessarily pose a direct threat to our planet.

These objects are typically located at enormous distances,

and the signals detected by scientists travel long distances through space before reaching Earth.

Such studies offer an opportunity to understand supermassive black holes and their role in the evolution of galaxies,

especially since cosmic jets can extend over vast distances and influence their surrounding environment.

The study underscores the importance of long-term astronomical observations,

as they allow for tracking changing cosmic phenomena and understanding their mechanisms more precisely.

Black holes remain among the most fascinating objects for astronomers and physicists.
